text:
- chief complaint: the patient presents for low back pain evaluation, with radiating left leg pain after bending to lift, plus follow-up of diabetes and hypertension.
- history of present illness: the patient developed sharp lower back pain radiating down the left leg about four days ago while bending to lift in the yard, without improvement. Intermittent tingling in certain positions; no bowel or bladder changes; no prior back surgery, with occasional prior back pain; ibuprofen partially helped. Diabetes is followed with home glucose readings of 120-140 mg/dL and HbA1c 7.1%. Blood pressure is controlled at home (120-130/70-80). Ankle swelling began 1-2 months after starting amlodipine.
- physical examination: no jugular venous distension, bruits, rales, or wheezing; 2/6 systolic ejection murmur (previously noted); regular rhythm; soft abdomen; left paraspinal lumbar tenderness; negative straight leg raise; normal reflexes and neurological exam; 1+ nonpitting bilateral lower extremity edema; no calf tenderness; negative Homans sign.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: low back pain radiating to the left leg, intermittent tingling, ankle swelling.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: naproxen 500 mg twice daily; cyclobenzaprine (Flexeril) 10 mg twice daily; hydrochlorothiazide 10 mg once daily; amlodipine (Norvasc) 5 mg daily discontinued.
- follow-up instructions: physical therapy referral; continue metformin 500 mg twice daily; repeat HbA1c, CBC, BMP, EKG, and chest X-ray ordered today; return in about two weeks to review results; lumbar X-ray if back pain does not improve.
